page.after:
What the differences mean

Plex's HDR-to-SDR tone mapping and scaling run as shaders on the iGPU's execution units, so EUs times clock is the hardware headroom that decides how many tone-mapped 4K streams a NAS can hold. It is a proxy, not a measured stream count: no named lab has published simultaneous 4K HEVC transcode counts for any of these units.

  • Shader budget (EU × GHz): N150 24 × 1.0 = 24.0; N95 16 × 1.2 = 19.2; N100 24 × 0.75 = 18.0; N5095 16 × 0.75 = 12.0; J4125 12 × 0.75 = 9.0. Figures from Intel ARK and Notebookcheck.
  • Price for the step up: F2-425 Plus N150 $499.99 − DXP2800 $389.99 = $110.00 for 33% more iGPU clock, two 5GbE ports and a third M.2 slot, if it comes back into stock. The $399.49 F2-425 Plus is the N95 model: $9.50 more than the DXP2800 for 8 fewer execution units.
  • Price per EU·GHz: F2-425 Plus N95 $399.49 / 19.2 = $20.81; F2-425 Plus N150 $499.99 / 24.0 = $20.83; DXP2800 $389.99 / 18.0 = $21.67; F2-425 $299.99 / 12.0 = $25.00; F4-425 $386.99 / 12.0 = $32.25; DS225+ $364.29 / 9.0 = $40.48, and that engine is unreachable on stock DSM.
  • Plex's two CPU floors: hardware tone mapping on Linux, Docker and NAS needs Kaby Lake or newer; HEVC output on a NAS needs Jasper Lake or newer. N100, N150 and N95 clear both. N5095 sits on the HEVC line. J4125 (Gemini Lake) is below it, so a Synology on the J4125 can only hardware-encode H.264 even when the iGPU works.
  • Every option needs a Plex Pass: Plex calls hardware-accelerated streaming a premium feature. Budget for it alongside the drives.

Stock firmware or a script: how each NAS reaches the Quick Sync engine

Plex talks to Intel Quick Sync through VA-API, which needs the Linux i915 kernel driver to expose the iGPU as /dev/dri/renderD128. Every CPU in the table has Quick Sync on Intel's spec page; the difference is whether the NAS operating system exposes it.

UGREEN DXP2800. UGOS Pro has no native Plex package (Plex's download list covers Synology, QNAP, ASUSTOR, TerraMaster, Netgear, Unraid, Thecus, Seagate and WD, not UGREEN), so Plex runs as a Docker container. Marius Hosting's guide, updated 2026-10-31 and tested with Plex 1.43.5, maps /dev/dri/renderD128 and /dev/dri/card0 into the container and then enables hardware transcoding and HDR tone mapping in Plex's transcoder settings. Plex calls the device mount an advanced setup, but it is a one-time compose entry that survives reboots and firmware updates. {buy:ugreen-nasync-dxp2800}

TerraMaster F2-425 Plus, F4-425, F2-425. Plex and Emby install from TerraMaster's app center (Starry Hope), and TerraMaster's spec sheet lists H.264 and H.265 hardware transcoding up to 4K at 60 fps. One caution: Plex's own download manifest (version 1.43.5, 2026-10-23) lists TerraMaster packages for TOS 4 and TOS 5 & 6 only. The N150 F2-425 Plus ships TOS 7 and the 425 series is moving to TOS 7, so check that the app center build installs on your TOS version before relying on it; Docker is the fallback.

Synology DS225+ and DS425+. Both use the J4125, the same chip that hardware-transcodes on the DS224+ and DS423+. On the x25 models Plex logs 'failed setup for format vaapi: hwaccel initialisation returned error'. In the Plex forum thread, Synology Technical Support replies quoted on 2025-09-10 and 2025-09-15 say hardware transcoding 'is not supported on these two models' and that for products released in 2025 and beyond Synology will no longer provide the kernel graphics driver required to enable it. Plex's Synology engineer ChuckPa wrote that without the kernel drivers to access the ASIC via i915 there is nothing Plex can do. Luka Manestar's Blackvoid workaround (published 2025-09-23, updated 2026-07-15) removes the stock i915, drm_kms_helper and drm modules over SSH as root and inserts 11 replacement modules compiled per DSM version; the steps must run after each reboot via Task Scheduler, and Manestar labels it unofficial and unsupported by Synology. A forum user adds that tone mapping on 2160p video is the one thing the workaround still cannot do.

Not recommended

  • Synology DS225+ and DS425+. Cheapest Intel Synology units, but the maker's own support says hardware transcoding is not supported, and the only route is a root-level module swap re-run at every boot and rebuilt for each DSM release.
  • Synology DS224+. Hardware transcoding works on its older DSM kernel, but the J4125 has half the execution units of the N100 and N150, cannot output HEVC under Plex's NAS rule, has two 1GbE ports and a 2-year warranty against 3 years on the DS225+.
  • UGREEN NASync DH2300 and DH4300 Plus. ARM processors with no Quick Sync engine, so Plex 4K is Direct Play only.
